misconceptions.description: Treating confident, fluent AI teaching advice as accurate without checking it against evidence or developmental appropriateness
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts or publishes AI advice because it sounds authoritative, without verifying its claims
misconceptions.feedback: Fluency is a style property, not an evidence check. Break the advice into claims and verify each one before it goes into the artifact or onto the page.

misconceptions.description: Treating the teacher persona as flavor text rather than a constraint that shapes tone, audience, and what the AI may assert
misconceptions.trigger: the persona block is present but the dialogue ignores its audience, knowledge bound, or hard stops
misconceptions.feedback: The persona is the contract the dialogue must honor. Check each AI turn against the persona's audience, knowledge bound, and hard stops, not just its mood.

misconceptions.description: Pasting the AI's first dialogue output as the finished artifact with no accepted, modified, and rejected trace
misconceptions.trigger: the submitted artifact is a single unedited AI draft with no accept/modify/reject log
misconceptions.feedback: One unedited draft shows no judgment. Keep the trace of what you accepted, modified, and rejected so a reviewer can audit the steering.
